title: Tet
hook: the first tet in the Torah is in tov, good (Genesis 1:4)

segments.voice: Yesterday, glasses raised and one word: l'chaim, to life. Your line was chet for life. What did you toast? Today ends the week, with a letter the rabbis were glad to dream about. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

Deep in the Talmud, in a tractate mostly about damages, oxen and pits and broken fences, the rabbis pause for something unexpected: dreams. What does it mean if you dream about a certain animal, a certain fruit, a certain letter of the alef-bet? Some of the answers are puzzling. One is beautiful. If you see the letter tet in a dream, they say, it's a good sign. And they don't leave it there. They give a reason, and the reason sends you all the way back to the first page of the Torah, to the very first morning of the world.
screen: `DREAMS, IN A BOOK OF DAMAGES.` → `A LETTER IN A DREAM.` → `TET IS A GOOD SIGN.`

segments.voice: Tet. Let's follow the rabbis' reason. The first stop is the first morning. God says let there be light, and there is light. And then, in the King James: "And God saw the light, that it was good." The Hebrew word for good is tov, and it begins with tet. In the Talmud, in tractate Bava Kamma, that's the whole argument: the first time the Torah uses a tet, it's in the word good. So a tet in your dream is good news. The second stop is the rest of that chapter. Good doesn't appear once and vanish. As the world is made, light, sea, land, plants, stars, animals, the chapter keeps stopping to say that God saw it was good. And at the end, looking at everything at once: "and, behold, it was very good." Tet keeps coming back like a refrain. The third stop is the week behind us, because today closes it. Seven letters, seven pictures. Gimel, running after someone in need. Dalet, a door, opened quietly. Heh, a breath, added to a name. Vav, a hook that joins. Zayin, remembering on purpose. Chet, a toast to life. And now tet, good. Lay them side by side and the alef-bet starts to read like a way of living. The last stop is your own week. Before anything else was finished, the text pauses over light and names it good. It doesn't wait for the whole creation to be done. Good can be noticed on the first morning of anything.
screen: `AND GOD SAW THE LIGHT.` · `TOV: GOOD, BEGINNING WITH TET.` · `GOOD, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `A WEEK OF LETTERS.` · then, large: `IT WAS GOOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: name something good. Settle, and breathe. Look back over this week, the way the first chapter of Genesis looks back over each day. Find one thing that was good. Not perfect. Good. A meal. A light through a window. A conversation that went better than you expected. Hold it in mind, and say to yourself, quietly: that was good. Then, if there's room, find one more. If you pray, you can give thanks for what you found. The bell holds the time.
Tet. The letter that begins tov, good, the word God says over the first light. Today's word.
Your line: tet for good. Today, say out loud that something is good, before it's finished. A meal, a draft, a day. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: The first chapter of Genesis, with its refrain that God saw it was good, is read in synagogue at the start of each yearly cycle of Torah readings; some teachers of the alef-bet introduce tet with the word tov.

fork.setup: you wake up and remember a dream: a single Hebrew letter, tet. you ask the rabbis of the Talmud what it means. what do they say?
options: a good sign: the first tet in the Torah is in good.
nothing: letters in dreams mean nothing.
fork.reveal: Bava Kamma calls it a good sign, and the reason is Genesis 1:4: "And God saw the light, that it was good." tov begins with tet.

original.note: Hebrew: good. It begins with tet (ט), the word God says over the first light.

trapdoor: what you thought: tet is just another t.
what it means: the letter that begins tov, good, said over the first light.

notes: Bava Kamma 55a paraphrased: one who sees tet in a dream, it is a good sign, because from the beginning of the Torah until 'And God saw the light that it was good' no tet appears. The claim 'first tet is in tov' is stated as the Talmud's argument, as the index requires. Confirm reference and paraphrase.
